audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer rates this HARD 7/10 and hands Swain the first five stages at 8/10, while the content layer chart gives Nasus stages 3-7 and Nasus wins 53.57% over 420 games.
audit.why: Two layers of the same level chart disagree on the same page. Swain has no dash and Wither is a point-and-click answer to a stand-still drain ultimate; the content-layer read matches the win rate.
audit.corrected: Aligned full-layer phases[0..6].side to the content chart (Skill, Skill, Nasus x5). diff/diffRating still read HARD 7/10 and should read EVEN 6/10, but I did not edit them because breakdown.difficulty and report[] carry the same number and report[] is not safely addressable — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer says how Nevermove actually works. The full layer only calls it 'a returning bolt that roots enemies it hits'; the content layer calls it an 'E pull into root' and has him rooting first and pulling second.
audit.why: Riot's own text: Swain launches a wave forward, it then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits, and he may then recast to pull rooted champions. The root is on the return leg, so the outgoing wave is safe to walk through and the dodge is on the way back. Getting that backwards is the single most common way a Nasus eats the full combo.
audit.corrected: Root lands on the return trip; sidestep the bolt coming back, not the throw. Cooldown 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/swain.json — E Nevermove description and cooldown

audit.whatIsWrong: Death's Hand is never named or explained anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Riot's text: the bolts pierce through enemies and enemies take more damage for each bolt that strikes them. A Nasus standing point-blank to last-hit eats several bolts instead of one, which is why his 'poke' feels like burst.
audit.corrected: Death’s Hand stacks damage per bolt that connects — do not stand where the full cone can land on you.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Demonic Ascension as the tracked cooldown and gave no numbers for anything.
audit.why: A 120s ultimate is not the lane clock. Nevermove at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s is the cooldown that decides whether Nasus can walk up, and Vision of Empire at 22/21/20/19/18s is how he gets a Soul Fragment from across the map.
audit.corrected: Real per-rank numbers for Nevermove and Vision of Empire now carry the section.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds anywhere, in either layer, in a matchup whose entire late game is a drain ultimate plus a passive that heals and permanently grows his max health.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals Swain from Soul Fragments and permanently raises his maximum health; Demonic Ascension drains health from everyone near him. A Nasus who out-grinds on Soul Eater lifesteal without anti-heal loses the exact fight he is built to win.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal is now called for before the committed all-in, at phases[3], phases[4], dosFull[0] and wants.foe[1].
sources: champ-data/_kits/swain.json — P and R heal flags

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged "Spirit Fire's" in `late` as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: False positive. Spirit Fire is Nasus's real E (champ-data/_kits/nasus.json). The checker matched the possessive form against the bare name.
audit.corrected: No change — the text is right.

notes: Difficulty labels for this matchup are wrong but I did not edit them: diff=HARD / diffRating=7/10 for a 53.57% Nasus matchup. Fixing them properly means changing diff, tone, diffRating AND breakdown.difficulty AND the 'Final Matchup Rating' entry inside report[], and I have no safe path expression for a single report[] element, so a partial fix would create a new contradiction on the page. This is champion-wide, not swain-specific: across nasus.full.js, diff is essentially uncorrelated with win rate (illaoi at 48.51% is FAVOURED, trundle at 56.63% is HARD, mel at 58.44% is HARD). Worth a single pass with a script rather than per-matchup edits.
